prompt: Which solvers should you use for optimization (OR-Tools, CPLEX, Gurobi)?
completion:
## Quick‑Start Decision Flow | Problem type | Typical size | Solver you’ll want to try first | Why it’s a good first stop | |---------------|--------------|---------------------------------|-----------------------------| | Small to medium LP/MIP (≤ 10 k variables, ≤ 50 k constraints) | • Academic / hobby | **OR‑Tools (CP‑SAT or CBC)** | Free, fast to prototype, great Python/Java/C++ APIs | | Large, enterprise‑grade MIP (hundreds of thousands of vars / constraints) | • Commercial | **Gurobi** (or CPLEX) | Highest throughput, best callbacks, advanced presolve, parallelism | | Mixed‑case (continuous + many integer decisions) | • Mixed | **Gurobi** (or CPLEX) | Handles huge MIP trees, highly robust | | Pure combinatorial / scheduling / routing | • 10‑100 k decisions | **OR‑Tools CP‑SAT** | Dedicated CP engine, no MIP tree blow‑up | | Quick “what‑if” exploratory modeling | • Rapid iteration | **OR‑Tools CBC** | Open‑source, easy to swap with commercial back‑end later | > **Bottom line**: *Start with OR‑Tools. If you hit performance, licensing, or advanced feature limits, switch to Gurobi or CPLEX.* --- ## What Is in Each Solver? | Solver | License | Core Engine | Language APIs | Feature Highlights | |--------|---------|-------------|---------------|--------------------| | **OR‑Tools** | Open source (Apache 2.0) | - CP‑SAT (constraint programming)
- CBC (mixed‑integer linear programming) | Python, Java, C++, Go, Rust, etc. | • Built‑in CP‑SAT with global constraints (All‑Different, No‑Overlap, Circuit, Flow, etc.)
• Fast, lightweight for small‑to‑medium problems
• Easy to embed in application code | | **CBC** (in OR‑Tools) | Open source (Apache 2.0) | Mixed‑integer linear programming | Same as OR‑Tools | • Free, decent performance for “toy” MIP
• No advanced callbacks | | **Gurobi** | Commercial (free academic & trial) | Cutting‑edge MIP, LP, QP, DP, etc. | Python, Java, C++, C#, MATLAB, R, Julia | • Top‑ranked speed, robust on huge instances
• Parallel (multi‑thread) by default
• Callback API (branch, cut, heuristic, node, solution)
• Presolve + strong branching
• Commercial support | | **IBM CPLEX** | Commercial (free academic & trial) | Same families as Gurobi | Python, Java, C++, C#, MATLAB, R, Julia | • Similar performance to Gurobi (often close)
• Deeply integrated into IBM ecosystem
• Advanced parameter tuning tools (CPLEX Optimizer) | --- ## How to Decide 1. **Problem nature** *LP, MIP, QP, DP, or combinatorial?* - If it’s *pure combinatorial*, start with CP‑SAT. - If it’s *continuous + integer*, a MIP engine is needed. 2. **Scale** - < 10 k vars → OR‑Tools (CBC or CP‑SAT) is usually enough. - > 10 k vars → Consider Gurobi or CPLEX; test on a smaller instance first. 3. **Speed vs. Cost** - OR‑Tools is free, but may be ~10‑30 % slower on large instances. - Gurobi’s cost per license is roughly $2 k–$12 k/year depending on usage, but it often pays back through faster solves. 4. **Advanced Features Needed?** - Custom heuristics or callbacks → Gurobi / CPLEX. - Parallelism beyond thread‑level (GPU, distributed) → Gurobi has GPU‑accelerated QP; CPLEX has a distributed mode. 5. **Licensing & Compliance** - Academic or non‑profit projects can use free academic licenses for both Gurobi and CPLEX. - Commercial use requires a paid license. 6. **Integration & Ecosystem** - If you’re already using IBM Cloud or other IBM products, CPLEX fits naturally. - Gurobi’s Python API is arguably the cleanest for quick prototypes. --- ## Practical Workflow 1. **Model** in OR‑Tools (Python/Java). ```python from ortools.linear_solver import pywraplp solver = pywraplp.Solver.CreateSolver('CBC') # add variables, constraints, objective solver.Solve() ``` 2. **Profile** – check solver time, memory, solution gap. 3. **If slow**: export the model in one of the standard formats (MPS, LP, CSV). 4. **Load** in Gurobi or CPLEX: ```python import gurobipy as gp m = gp.read('model.lp') m.optimize() ``` 5. **Tune** – use solver parameters, presolve, mipgap, node limit, etc. 6. **Optional**: use Gurobi’s `callback` to implement a custom heuristic or to log node information. --- ## Quick Reference Cheat‑Sheet | Use Case | Solver | Best‑Fit Feature | Notes | |----------|--------|------------------|-------| | “Just solve a linear program” | OR‑Tools (CBC) | Lightweight | Free, good for quick checks | | Large‑scale MIP with > 100 k vars | Gurobi | Parallelism, callbacks | Fastest on many benchmarks | | Need strong presolve + advanced branching | CPLEX | Deep branching heuristics | Similar speed, better support in some IBM environments | | Scheduling with “All‑Different” or “No‑Overlap” | OR‑Tools CP‑SAT | Dedicated CP constraints | Avoid MIP blow‑up | | Want to keep everything open source | OR‑Tools + CBC | Entire stack open | No commercial license needed | --- ## Bottom‑Line Takeaway - **Start free** with **OR‑Tools**. It gives you a full CP engine and a light MIP back‑end. - **If you hit the wall** (time > minutes, memory > GBs, need custom callbacks), **switch to Gurobi**. It’s consistently the fastest commercial solver for most MIP workloads. - **Use CPLEX** if you’re already embedded in IBM’s ecosystem or need the subtle performance edge on very particular problem structures (e.g., many network flow constraints). Testing a *single* small instance on each solver will give you a realistic sense of speed and memory usage. From there, you can scale up and decide which engine gives you the best ROI for your project. Happy modeling!
